method: Independent manual review of saved answers, drafts, verifier feedback, action chronology and cited passages; local Corpus text/hash/outline validation; offline SDK signature inspection and AST parsing only. No model calls, network/backend calls, browser control or source edits.
pass_definition: Useful pass means the original planned task checks are met; material caveats are reported separately. A source-check pass is not a proof that every sentence or unexecuted example is correct.

sdk_check.scope: Signature compatibility and local source inspection only; source version refers to the SDK reference page, not all guides. No SDK example or provider call was executed.

findings.answer_claim: In Python all four work as context managers. On exit they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions.
findings.evidence: S2 itself uses this wording immediately after the table says Conversation has no span. Installed Conversation docstring also states no span.
findings.assessment: The preceding no-span mapping is correct. A clearer explanation would say span-producing contexts end their spans, while the conversation context groups turns and manages current context. This ambiguity is inherited from the source, not an invented API.

The example records prompt/output totals and concrete response_model, but drops cache_read_input_tokens from the source quickstart. S5 says cache reads/writes must be supplied in addition to total input. Tracing and history still work; cached-cost breakdown can be inaccurate. The response should either retain the documented cache field or omit the optional detailed cost promise.
